title: TEXTBEFORE and TEXTAFTER: split on a delimiter

docs.syntax: =TEXTBEFORE(text,"-") keeps what precedes the delimiter; =TEXTAFTER keeps what follows
docs.explain:
TEXTBEFORE and TEXTAFTER split a cell on a delimiter, one function per side. You name the delimiter as a piece of text, so no position number appears anywhere in the formula. Each returns the half on its side and drops the delimiter itself.

The formula =TEXTBEFORE(A2,"-") returns ORD from the code ORD-4471, and TEXTAFTER with the same arguments returns 4471. Move both formulas to a column of five-letter prefixes and they keep working, because the delimiter still marks the join.

When the delimiter is missing, both functions return #N/A instead of inventing a half. A code that does not fit the pattern is exactly the row you want to see fail, since a blank answer would hide it. Read the error as a prompt to clean that row, not as a fault in the formula.

errors.text: The cell holds no copy of the delimiter, which leaves no place to split.
The workbook was built in an Excel version older than the one that added these functions.
The two functions differ by one word, and the wrong one returns the other half of the code.

docs.atWork: Separating an order prefix from its number without counting characters.
docs.outcome: Split a code at its delimiter, taking either the part before or the part after.
docs.teaches: TEXTBEFORE and TEXTAFTER naming the delimiter instead of a position
docs.dataset: Order codes: a three-letter prefix, a hyphen, a number

screens.prompt: In B2, read the three letters before the hyphen in the order code in A2.

hints.syntax: =TEXTBEFORE(A2,"-"): the code, then the delimiter in quotes.
hints.func-textbefore: The prefix is everything before the hyphen, which is what TEXTBEFORE answers.
hints.require-ref: The order code is in A2.
hints.value: Everything before the hyphen is ORD.
hints.error: A code with no hyphen returns #N/A, and the grader reports it as an error rather than a wrong value.

reject.why: counting three characters breaks the moment the prefix changes length
splitting on the first four characters keeps the hyphen
the answer picks up a trailing space
the prefix is upper case in the code
the formula reads the second row rather than A2
the code holds only one hyphen
there is no underscore to split on
the code is typed in rather than read from A2
the arguments fall outside the parentheses

screens.prompt: In B2, read the four digits after the hyphen in the order code in A2.

hints.syntax: =TEXTAFTER(A2,"-"): the code, then the delimiter in quotes.
hints.func-textafter: The number sits after the hyphen, which is TEXTAFTER's half.
hints.require-ref: The order code is in A2.
hints.error: The grader looks for TEXTAFTER, so TEXTBEFORE returns ORD and fails the function rule.

reject.why: counting four characters from the right breaks on a shorter number
splitting on the prefix keeps the hyphen in the answer

seo.title: TEXTBEFORE and TEXTAFTER in Excel
seo.description: Name the delimiter and Excel keeps the half on your side of it, with no position to work out. No delimiter in the cell means #N/A, not a silent blank.
